title: BGN regime-gamma at g0235's multipliers, switching 4x FASTER
question: Does a rolling window capture more of the regime premium when regimes turn over many times inside it?
notes:
B1-fast. IDENTICAL to var-bgn_gam-g0235-v2 except the two switch probabilities, scaled by 4: p01 0.25/12 -> 1/12 and p10 0.50/12 -> 2/12. The STATIONARY STRESS SHARE IS UNCHANGED at exactly 1/3 (p01/(p01+p10)), and gmult is unchanged at [0.2, 3.5], so the cross-section, the premia and the whole-sample constant-theta ceilings are the same economy seen at a different speed: calm spells 12 months instead of 48, stress spells 6 instead of 24, about 40 switches inside a 360-month estimation window instead of 10. PREDICTION: room (a constant-theta, whole-sample quantity that depends on the stationary mix, not the path) is unchanged within seed noise; the LINEAR methods lose ground because a window average blends the two regimes ever more finely; DKKM holds if the exported regime feature lets it condition; so the proportional gap rises. If room moves materially, the claim that it depends only on the stationary mix is wrong and that is the more interesting result. Paired with var-bgn_gam-g0235s-v1 (4x slower) as a speed ladder.
